body:
Thanks for working on this — hitting this exact limitation in production.

I maintain a VR streaming emulator (medical-imaging startup, Godot 4.6 desktop Windows) that needs to import a D3D11 `SHARED_NTHANDLE` texture produced by a Rust sidecar (Media Foundation H.264 decode → D3D11 shared texture with `KEYEDMUTEX`). The intended consumer path is `Texture2DRD` via Vulkan external-memory import.

Ran a feasibility spike this week — the NVIDIA driver advertises `VK_KHR_external_memory_win32` + `VK_KHR_win32_keyed_mutex`, but Godot 4.6's `VkDevice` isn't created with them and `vkGetDeviceProcAddr` refuses to return the related function pointers. Exactly the gap this PR closes.

We currently fall back to `CopyResource` + `Map` + `texture_update` (~10 ms at 1080p). This PR's `additional_device_extensions` hook would let us move to true zero-copy — the `texture_create_from_extension` path is already reachable from a GDExtension in 4.6, only the device-creation extension list is blocking.

+1 from a real production use case. Happy to test a pre-release build against our integration if that's useful.

Hi, I'm working on a live graphics broadcast software and we're trying to make a bridge to render the Godot scene with depth/matte into our renderer and overlay it with other media/scene/camera sources. I built this branch and tested locally and it worked well for us. We are probably going to ship it to our customers to use Godot as a option for making 3D scenes as soon as this gets merged into master. Thanks!

Ps. For anyone needing these vulkan extensions there is a bit of a dumb workaround until this gets merged. Enabling OpenXR and starting SteamVR with edited settings to not require a HDM will enable a lot of them automatically. Not something to ship stuff with but good enough for development, at least if you don't feel like building this branch.

Tested this PR on real hardware against a GDExtension that does hardware video decode (Media Foundation → D3D11 NV12 textures) and presents zero-copy into Godot via `VK_KHR_external_memory_win32`:

- Platform: Windows 11, AMD Radeon RX Vega (Vulkan 1.3.260), Forward+
- Build: this PR's head (`ebc9266`, merge with master), MSVC 2022
- Setting used:
  ```ini
  [rendering]
  rendering_device/vulkan/additional_device_extensions=PackedStringArray("VK_KHR_external_memory_win32", "VK_KHR_win32_keyed_mutex")
  ```

It works great! With the setting present, both extensions are enabled on the device, `vkGetDeviceProcAddr` resolves `vkGetMemoryWin32HandlePropertiesKHR`, and the full interop chain runs: D3D11 shared NT handle → `vkAllocateMemory` (dedicated import) → multi-planar NV12 `VkImage` → `RenderingDevice::texture_create_from_extension` → compute NV12→RGB → `Texture2DRD`. Hardware-decoded video renders correctly, no CPU copy. On stock Godot the same code hard-fails at device-extension gating, so this PR is exactly the missing mechanism. The unsupported-extension case degrades gracefully, as described.

One adjacent gap worth noting (likely out of scope for this PR): `texture_create_from_extension` hardcodes `VK_IMAGE_ASPECT_COLOR_BIT` for the view it creates, but per-plane views of a multi-planar image (e.g. R8/RG8 views of `VK_FORMAT_G8_B8R8_2PLANE_420_UNORM` NV12) require `VK_IMAGE_ASPECT_PLANE_0_BIT`/`PLANE_1_BIT`. With COLOR aspect the driver aliases plane-0 memory and output is garbage. I verified the end-to-end path renders pixel-correct with a small local engine patch mapping the view aspect to the plane, so an explicit plane/aspect parameter on `texture_create_from_extension` would cover the planar video case. I can open a proposal for that separately.

Thanks @dsh0416. This unblocks a real use case.

Another real-world data point for this PR, this time from the synchronization side rather than the memory side.

My project runs Godot's Forward Mobile renderer on XREAL AR glasses. XREAL's native graphics library, the vendor runtime that drives the glasses, composites through GL and consumes client GL texture names, so a GDExtension shares each Vulkan eye image with GL through `VK_KHR_external_memory_fd` + `GL_EXT_memory_object_fd`. That half already works on stock Godot. The missing half was synchronization: nothing could make the GL compositor wait for the Vulkan copy, because exporting a semaphore needs `VK_KHR_external_semaphore_fd` enabled at device creation and stock Godot never requests it. In practice that meant choosing between tearing under head motion and a `vkQueueWaitIdle` every frame.

To try this PR I backported it onto 4.7.2-rc, rebuilt the editor and the Android export template, and listed `VK_KHR_external_semaphore_fd` in `rendering/rendering_device/vulkan/additional_device_extensions`. On device (XREAL Beam Pro, Android 14, Adreno 710, driving One Pro glasses) `vkGetSemaphoreFdKHR` now resolves, and the sync path I could not build before simply works: signal an exportable `VkSemaphore` on the copy submission, export it as a `SYNC_FD`, wrap it with `EGL_ANDROID_native_fence_sync`, and issue a server-side `eglWaitSyncKHR` before the frame reaches the compositor. Head-motion tearing is gone, and the frame rate went from 51-58 FPS under the wait-idle workaround to a steady 60, verified by flipping between the two sync modes at runtime. A stock template still leaves the extension off and the function pointer null, so absence stays silent and safe, which is what the optional registration promises.

godotengine/godot-proposals#15210 asks for a similar capability with a fixed list of external-memory extensions, semaphores as an optional extra. I prefer this PR's approach: the setting covers the synchronization half of interop as well as the memory half, and it extends to future interop extensions without further engine changes.

Hoping this lands - for us it turns a 13% frame-rate tax into one line of project settings. Thanks @dsh0416.

Adding a concrete use case in support of this PR, coming from #122335 which I closed in its favor.

I ship a Godot 4.5 arcade frontend on Windows that does zero-copy hardware video decode: a D3D11VA decoded frame is converted on the GPU into a shared D3D11 texture, imported into Vulkan with `VK_KHR_external_memory_win32`, and wrapped with `RenderingDevice.texture_create_from_extension()`. The frame never touches the CPU. On my machine that removes about 5 ms of per-frame copying at 1080p60, roughly a third of a core during video playback. I currently maintain a custom engine build solely to enable that extension (plus `VK_KHR_external_semaphore_win32` for fence sharing), and this PR would let me do it with a project setting on stock Godot instead.

Two notes from building that pipeline against a hand-patched device, in case they are useful here:
- The query API is the important half. GDExtension code needs a reliable way to know the extension is genuinely enabled on the device. Resolving the extension function through `vkGetDeviceProcAddr` and getting null is the failure mode on an unpatched device, and calling through an instance-level trampoline instead segfaults, so an explicit query is much friendlier than what extension authors have today.
- Registering requested extensions as optional is the right call. My interop falls back to a CPU copy path when the import is unavailable, and optional registration means the same project file runs everywhere.

Happy to test this PR against a real consumer: I can build it and run the full zero-copy pipeline plus fallback matrix on Windows 11 with NVIDIA hardware and report results here.
